comments: KuRALSNetNPUSeg: phase 1 of dropping the CenterNet head (v25-v32 all regressed/collapsed on top of v24's heatmap+offset detection head -- see kuralsnet_npu.json's comments). Reuses v24's exact NPU-legal backbone through dec_a (/2 resolution, 24ch) but replaces head_out with a plain per-pixel segmentation head (n_classes logits, argmax decode off-NPU), matching baseline kuralsnet's task formulation and training recipe (this config is copied from kuralsnet.json almost verbatim -- nb_epochs=300, custom_loss=nbs1/NBSLoss, lr=0.0001, cos/Tmax=300 -- specifically to isolate architecture from training-budget as a confound when comparing against baseline's on-record UAV precision/recall of 81.80%/94.83%). Stays at /2 resolution rather than baseline's native /1: v21-v24 already proved /1 reopens a real decoder-upsample-chain activation-magnitude collapse risk that a per-tensor quantization scale can't correct, and phase 1 should isolate whether the segmentation task formulation itself (dense per-pixel supervision, no CenterNet threshold/plateau calibration problem) fixes v24's false-alarm-rate problem before also reopening that risk. kurals/learners/model.py (the shared segmentation trainer) had no QAT lifecycle at all -- added quant_warmup_iters/quant_freeze_iters support there, gated behind hasattr(net, 'set_quant_enabled') so every other registered model's behavior is unchanged. First attempt used quant_warmup_iters=500/quant_freeze_iters=15000 (scaled from v24's 5000 to preserve the same ~15% freeze fraction of this recipe's 3x-longer, 103200-iteration budget) -- result: collapsed to predicting background everywhere, confirmed via three consecutive validation checks (epochs 2/4/6) with bit-identical Prec=mIoU=0.24999.../Dice=0.24999... while train loss kept dropping (the same 'loss looks fine but network found a trivial degenerate minimum' signature as this project's very first collapse, v4). Diagnosed with a 15-epoch float-only diagnostic (quant_warmup_iters set effectively infinite): without QAT, the identical model showed real if noisy learning (Val mIoU 0.1785->0.1928->0.1977->0.1939, Test mIoU 0.1733->0.1882->0.1932->0.2014 across epochs 2/4/6/8, clearly diverging metrics rather than the frozen collapse's bit-identical ones) -- ruling out model capacity/architecture as the cause and pointing squarely at QAT's introduction at iteration 500 (only ~1.5 epochs in, before the model had learned any non-trivial foreground signal) as the trigger: quantization noise arriving that early apparently knocked an undertrained network into the trivial-background local minimum it then couldn't escape. quant_warmup_iters raised 500->15000 (~14.5% of the budget, ~43 epochs of pure float32 training -- extrapolating from the diagnostic's still-rising trend at epoch 8, this should be enough runway to reach a solid non-degenerate solution first) and quant_freeze_iters raised 15000->60000 (~58%, preserving a large ~45000-iteration QAT-active calibration window between warmup and freeze, plus ~43200 iterations/~125 epochs of weight-only adaptation afterward). Not yet retrained with this schedule -- result to be appended here once phase 1 completes.
